Europe's hydrogen core engine — every Ariane 5 depended on it

Vulcain 2 was the engine Europe built to achieve independent access to geostationary orbit. Developed by Snecma under ESA's Ariane 5 program, it runs a gas-generator cycle on LOX and LH2, powering the cryogenic main stage from liftoff through main-engine cutoff while the solid boosters do the heavy lifting of the first minutes. Its December 2002 debut was lost to a nozzle-cooling failure that destroyed the vehicle; after redesign it flew successfully from 2005 and became the reliable heart of Ariane 5 through the rocket's final flight in July 2023, placing satellites and interplanetary probes — including JWST — on their trajectories.
